newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt nudges higher, awaits Ifo figures.
newsitem.headline: German debt nudges higher, awaits Ifo figures.

text.p: German debt nudged higher in early Thursday trading, supported by U.S. Treasury gains on Wednesday, but traders said activity would be range-bound until at least mid-morning when the German Ifo index is released.
"In 45 minutes we will know a little bit more about what might happen today," a dealer at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.

By 0724 GMT the September Bund futures contract traded on Frankfurt's DTB was up 14 basis points at 101.47 while the 10-year cash bond was at 102.10 copared with with Wednesday's closing proce of 102.12.
The Ifo index is scheduled to be released at 0800 GMT.
But dealers said the market had largely priced in a west German business climate index of 95 and that only a massive move away from that number would shake the market out of its expected range.

"The figure is largely priced in anyway," said another dealer, adding that even the Bundesbank's talks with Bonn about currency reserve revaluations were no longer capturing the market's full attention.
"The market now needs to find something new to focus on," the dealer at Deutsche said. Dealers for the day expected a trading range from 101.64 to 101.26 for the futures contract.
Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer is scheduled to speak again on Thursday, but here too dealers largely expected him to reiterate the need for a strong euro.
